description:
FILED s449 (Fable, round-7 review of agent Q).  PRE-EXISTING family behaviour; #592 just made fcntl exist so the shape became reachable.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
    my $dead;                              # never opened (or: close(my $dead))
    my $r = fcntl($dead, 1, 0);            # perl: DIES "Bad symbol for filehandle", rc 9
                                           # PCL:  undef, $! = EBADF, runs on
    open(my $fh, "<", $f); close $fh;
    fcntl($fh, 1, 0);                      # perl: undef + EBADF -- PCL identical (probed s449)

So the CLOSED-handle arm is right and the UNDEF-lexical arm is conflated into it: %p-fcntl-impl (and possibly siblings that resolve a handle then test null) answer the closed-handle way for a value that was never a handle.  #529 established the rule for fileno (undef for any non-open handle -- and that WAS probed right); fcntl is a different builtin in perl: it DIES on an unopened symbol/undef.  SURVEY FIRST: which handle builtins die on undef vs return false (fcntl dies; fileno does not; probe ioctl/flock/binmode/truncate before touching anything) -- one shared discriminator at the resolver, not per-builtin patches (rule 11).  BAR: per-builtin probe table vs perl, the die text perl-shaped, Pl/t rows for the die and the false member each.
subject: fcntl (and family?) on a NEVER-OPENED lexical dies "Bad symbol for filehandle" in perl; PCL answers undef+EBADF -- perl's two negative answers are different facts (the #529 lesson again)
